mainEntity.name: How much does a Ford Galaxy 2.0 TDCi EcoBlue engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost depends on the engine's condition. A used Ford Galaxy 2.0 TDCi EcoBlue engine typically costs £500-£1,200, while a reconditioned unit ranges from £1,500-£2,800. A fully rebuilt engine with a warranty costs £2,500-£4,000 (supply only).

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of EGR or DPF failure in a Ford Galaxy 2.0 TDCi EcoBlue?

acceptedAnswer.text: EGR or DPF failure in the Ford Galaxy 2.0 TDCi EcoBlue usually presents gradually before causing a complete breakdown.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an older Ford Galaxy 2.0 TDCi EcoBlue?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's current market value. If your Ford Galaxy 2.0 TDCi EcoBlue is worth under £6,000, a full rebuilt engine replacement may exceed the car's value, making a used engine or scrap evaluation more sensible. For vehicles valued over £8,000, a reconditioned engine with a warranty is a financially sound investment.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Ford Galaxy 2.0 TDCi EcoBlue engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard Ford Galaxy 2.0 TDCi EcoBlue engine swap typically takes 1 to 2 days once the replacement unit is on-site.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the UKWA and TXWA Ford Galaxy 2.0 TDCi EcoBlue engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are 2.0L Duratorq/EcoBlue diesel engines producing 150 PS. The UKWA was used in earlier Mk3 models (2015-2018) with Euro 5 compliance, while the TXWA features updated engine management and Euro 6d-TEMP emissions compliance for the Mk3 facelift (2018-2020).

historyTimeline.h2: Ford Galaxy 2.0 TDCi EcoBlue - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: Introduced as the refined, efficient diesel workhorse of the Galaxy range, the 2.0 TDCi EcoBlue variant replaced the earlier Duratorq units with improved emissions compliance and enhanced fuel economy for modern family MPV use.

milestones.description: UKWA introduced, 2.0L Duratorq TDCi (150 PS), established as the core diesel option for the Mk3 Galaxy with Euro 5 compliance.
TXWA introduced, 2.0L EcoBlue TDCi (150 PS), featuring updated engine management and Euro 6d-TEMP emissions compliance for the Mk3 facelift.
QXWA introduced, 2.0L EcoBlue TDCi (150 PS), refined for improved NVH and fuel economy with AdBlue compatibility for Euro 6d compliance.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Ford Galaxy 2.0 TDCi EcoBlue is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

problems.h4: EGR & DPF Clogging - Why the Ford Galaxy 2.0 TDCi EcoBlue Loses Power
problems.affectedModels: Ford Galaxy 2.0 TDCi EcoBlue (UKWA, TXWA, QXWA, BNBA, 2015-present)
problems.rootCause: Urban driving prevents the DPF from completing regeneration cycles, leading to excessive soot buildup. This backpressure, combined with EGR valve clogging, causes rough idling, misfires, and eventual limp mode.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chemical DPF clean and EGR valve inspection/cleaning.
repairOptions.longevity: Temporary fix; does not resolve underlying mechanical wear if severe.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call when multiple components (injectors, turbo, DPF) are failing simultaneously.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Ford Galaxy 2.0 TDCi EcoBlue (Mk3) is currently valued between £6,000 and £18,000 depending on year and condition [THIRD-PARTY]. - Vehicle worth under ~£6,000: repair or a used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£6,000-£10,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£10,000-£18,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. If your Ford Galaxy 2.0 TDCi EcoBlue is valued under £6,000, a full rebuilt engine replacement cost risks exceeding the vehicle's value. Evaluate scrap or part-exchange value first.
problems.recommendation: If the issue is isolated to a clogged DPF or EGR, a specialist clean is cost-effective. However, if you are facing concurrent injector, turbo, and DPF failures, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine is the most financially sound long-term solution.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt Ford Galaxy 2.0 TDCi EcoBlue engine prices

problems.h4: Turbocharger Wear - Why the Ford Galaxy 2.0 TDCi EcoBlue Enters Limp Mode
problems.affectedModels: Ford Galaxy 2.0 TDCi EcoBlue (UKWA, TXWA, QXWA, 2015-present)
problems.rootCause: The variable geometry turbocharger actuator linkages are prone to carbon buildup and seizing, triggering an overboost or underboost fault code and restricting engine power.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing the electronic actuator and cleaning the linkage.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if the turbo core itself is undamaged and spinning freely.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if turbo failure has sent metal debris into the engine or intercooler.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a £8,000 Ford Galaxy 2.0 TDCi EcoBlue, a £400 specialist turbo repair is viable, but a £3,000+ engine replacement requires careful evaluation against the vehicle's current market value. If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing.
problems.recommendation: Always have the turbo core inspected before replacing just the actuator. If the turbo shaft has play or the intercooler is contaminated with oil/debris, a full engine replacement is safer to prevent rapid secondary failure.
